definition.title: Telescope Builder
learning_objectives: Explain the distinct roles of aperture, telescope focal length, focal ratio, eyepiece focal length, and eyepiece apparent field.
Calculate and interpret magnification, approximate true field of view, and exit pupil.
Show that aperture, rather than eyepiece magnification, sets the idealized diffraction and empirical resolving references and geometric collecting-area ratio.
Show how an idealized Barlow or focal reducer changes effective focal length, effective focal ratio, magnification, approximate true field, and exit pupil.
Compare a supplied scalar target angular extent with the approximate field diameter without claiming brightness, resolution, framing quality, or observability.
Recognize practical visual-observing warnings as rules of thumb rather than physical hard limits or guaranteed outcomes.

fields.name: aperture_mm
fields.meaning: Clear nominal objective diameter supplied to the idealized model.

fields.name: telescope_type
fields.meaning: Descriptive telescope design label; it is numeric-output invariant in v1.

fields.name: eyepiece_apparent_field_deg
fields.meaning: Nominal apparent angular field supplied by the hypothetical eyepiece.

fields.name: optical_modifier_kind
fields.meaning: At most one idealized effective focal-length modifier.

fields.name: optical_modifier_factor
fields.meaning: Assumed effective focal-length multiplier produced by the optical train.

fields.name: target_angular_size_arcmin
fields.meaning: One characteristic scalar angular diameter or extent for field comparison.

input_schema.invalid_handling: Reject non-finite values, booleans in numeric fields, unknown enums, inconsistent modifiers, out-of-range values, native focal ratios outside 2 to 30, magnification below 1x, and unsupported serialized state without calculating.

relationships: Effective focal length is native focal length multiplied by the supplied effective modifier factor.
Native and effective focal ratios divide the corresponding focal length by aperture.
Magnification uses effective telescope focal length divided by eyepiece focal length.
Approximate true field divides eyepiece apparent field by magnification.
Exit pupil divides aperture by magnification.
Dawes and Rayleigh are aperture-only ideal/reference quantities in this model.
Geometric collecting-area ratio versus a 7 mm reference pupil is proportional to aperture squared.
Target field fraction is target angular size in degrees divided by approximate true field.

equations.rayleigh_limit: theta_R = 1.22 * lambda / D radians, with lambda = 550 nm, converted to arcseconds

calculation_module.valid_domain: Python double-precision arithmetic over finite validated continuous inputs, supported telescope/modifier enums, native focal ratio 2 through 30, and derived magnification at least 1x.
calculation_module.numerical_policy: Use deterministic double precision. Use Astropy units for the Rayleigh wavelength conversion. Internal values are not rounded; displayed values are presentation formatting. Arithmetic tolerances are 1e-12 relative for ratios, 1e-9 mm for lengths, and 1e-9 in the relevant angular unit.

output_schema: Dawes empirical visual double-star reference in arcseconds
Rayleigh clear-circular-aperture diffraction reference in arcseconds
ideal collecting-area ratio versus a 7 mm reference pupil
target angular size in degrees and target field fraction
warning_semantics: high_magnification_guideline: emit only when magnification is greater than 2.0 times aperture in millimetres; this is a common visual rule of thumb, not a maximum.
very_small_exit_pupil: emit only when exit pupil is less than 0.5 mm; this is a difficult visual-observing regime, not an impossibility claim.
exit_pupil_exceeds_reference_pupil: emit only when exit pupil is greater than the 7.0 mm reference pupil; this does not claim every observer has a 7.0 mm pupil.
Warnings do not invalidate a configuration and no warnings are generated for unmodelled seeing, mount, quality, brightness, or target properties.
definition.telescope_type_disclosure: Telescope type is descriptive in Telescope Builder v1. The model does not know this instrument's obstruction, transmission, aberrations, or optical quality, so the numeric estimates use the same ideal clear-aperture geometry as the other types. A refractor selection does not imply perfect transmission or absence of aberration.
definition.modifier_semantics: The modifier factor is the supplied effective focal-length multiplier actually produced by the optical train. Lumina does not derive it from lens spacing; real Barlow and reducer factors can vary with optical spacing and equipment design.
definition.target_fit_definition: fits means only that the supplied scalar target angular extent is no larger than the approximate field diameter. It does not mean visible, resolved, bright enough, aesthetically framed, or observable.
definition.visualization_module: Semantic HTML and accessible SVG render a schematic optical train and a proportional field-fit comparison from canonical outputs. Drawings are normalized or schematic, not prescriptions or physical scale; the textual result is authoritative and no visual transform changes the science.
assumptions: The telescope is an idealized thin or first-order visual optical system.
Aperture and focal lengths are exact supplied model inputs in millimetres.
There is one eyepiece and at most one effective focal-length modifier.
The supplied modifier factor is already the effective factor, and supplied apparent field is nominal.
Dawes, Rayleigh, and collecting-area quantities use clear-circular-aperture reference geometry.
Rayleigh uses a 550 nm reference wavelength.
Collecting-area comparison and the large-exit-pupil warning use a 7 mm reference pupil.
limitations: This is an idealized visual-observing geometry model, not a real-equipment recommender or guaranteed-view calculator.
Dawes is an empirical visual double-star reference, not a general detail threshold or seeing prediction.
Rayleigh is a clear-circular-aperture diffraction reference and ignores seeing, obstruction, aberration, optical quality, detector sampling, and observer acuity.
Ideal collecting area ignores transmission, reflectivity, obstruction, coatings, vignetting, and eye sensitivity; do not read it as a brightness multiplier.
Approximate true field uses AFOV divided by magnification because field-stop diameter and distortion are not model inputs.
The target is a scalar angular extent only; fit does not imply brightness, resolution, morphology, framing quality, or observability.
The model does not include seeing, transparency, sky brightness, target magnitude or surface brightness, mount behavior, tracking, imaging, cameras, or any excluded optical/equipment variable.
Practical warnings are rules of thumb whose real usefulness depends on optics, atmosphere, target, and observer.

validation_fixtures.purpose: A 2x effective focal-length multiplier changes focal-length-derived outputs only.
A 0.5x effective focal-length multiplier widens the approximate field.
Doubling aperture at fixed native focal length and eyepiece preserves magnification and field while scaling aperture references.
A valid high-power configuration emits both strict-inequality practical warnings.
Exact 2x-per-mm and 0.5 mm exit-pupil boundaries do not warn.
A valid exit pupil larger than the reference pupil emits the large-pupil context warning.
A target extent larger than the approximate field receives only the narrow geometric non-fit classification.
Descriptive telescope type changes no numeric output or warning code.

scientific_validation.method: Known-case expected values are checked as reviewed literal fixtures, not recomputed by a second production formula. Independent reference review confirms the first-order telescope relationships and the restricted interpretations of Dawes, Rayleigh, field, exit pupil, and practical magnification.
